facts.statement: Neuquenornis fossils date to the Santonian age, approximately 85 to 83 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in the Santonian Bajo de la Carpa Formation, dating from about 85-83 million years ago.

facts.statement: Neuquenornis had a tarsometatarsus measuring 46.8 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: This was a sizeable bird for its time, with a tarsometatarsus 46.8mm long.

facts.statement: Informal estimates place the length of Neuquenornis at nearly 30 centimeters, excluding the tail.
facts.quote: Informal estimates suggest that it measured nearly 30 cm (12 in) in length excluding the tail.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil indicates a length of 23.5 cm, a hip height of 17 cm, and a weight of 205 grams.
facts.quote: MUCPv-142, a skull and a partial postcranial remains, indicates an animal with a length of 23.5 cm, hip height of 17 cm, and weight of 205 g.

facts.statement: Neuquenornis possessed long legs with hooked claws adapted for perching and foraging on the ground or in shallow water.
facts.quote: Long legs with hooked claws were well suited for perching as well as for gathering food on ground or shallow water.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Neuquenornis lived in nesting colonies and buried its eggs in a behavior similar to megapodes.
facts.quote: A nesting colony has been attributed to this bird, showcasing that it display megapode-like egg burial behaviour.

facts.statement: The species was formally described by Chiappe and Calvo in 1994.
facts.quote: N. volans was described by Chiappe and Calvo in 1994.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is cataloged as MUCPv-142.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil is catalogued as MUCPv-142.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil is housed in the collection of the Museo de Ciencias Naturales at the Universidad Nacional del Comahue in Neuquen, Argentina.
facts.quote: It is in the collection of the Museo de Ciencias Naturales, Universidad Nacional del Comahue, Neuquen, Argentina.

facts.statement: Chiappe and Calvo originally classified Neuquenornis in the family Avisauridae within the Enantiornithiformes.
facts.quote: Chiappe and Calvo (1994) placed N. volans in the Family Avisauridae, near Avisaurus in the Enantiornithiformes.

facts.statement: Recent unpublished analyses suggest Neuquenornis may be more closely related to Concornis and Cathayornis than previously thought.
facts.quote: A more recent, unpublished, unreviewed, analysis that includes many newly described Enantiornithes finds it closer to Concornis and Cathayornis (or Sinornis).

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation, which dates to the Santonian stage between 85 and 83 million years ago.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles fueron hallados en la formación Bajo de la Carpa, que data de hace entre 85-83 millones de años (Santoniense).

facts.statement: The time range for Neuquenornis is restricted to the Santonian, from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)
